When each row already describes a point, pass the table straight to `hchart()`.
Use a `data_to_*` helper when you need to calculate boxplot statistics, count
transitions or reorganize rows into the structure a chart expects.

| What you have | Helper | What to do with the result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Several measurements per observation | `data_to_parallel_coordinates()` | Add one line per row with `hc_add_series_list()`. |
| A numeric measurement and optional groups | `data_to_boxplot()` | Add the boxes and optional outlier series with `hc_add_series_list()`. |
| One column per stage in a journey | `data_to_sankey()` | Pass the weighted links to `hchart(links, type = "sankey")`. |
| Nested groups and a numeric size | `data_to_hierarchical()` | Pass the nodes to `hchart(nodes, type = "treemap")` or `hchart(nodes, type = "sunburst")`. |
| Coordinates and text for labels | `data_to_annotation_labels()` | Pass the labels to `hc_add_annotation()` on an existing chart. |

```{r setup, message=FALSE}
library(highcharter)
```

## Parallel coordinates

Each flower in `iris` becomes a line crossing four measurement axes.
Select the numeric columns in display order. Use the species to name and
color the lines. This replaces the former `hcparcords(iris, ...)` call.

```{r parallel-coordinates}
measurements <- iris[1:4]
series <- data_to_parallel_coordinates(
  measurements,
  name = as.character(iris$Species),
  color = colorize(iris$Species)
)

highchart() |>
  hc_chart(type = "line", parallelCoordinates = TRUE) |>
  hc_xAxis(categories = names(measurements)) |>
  hc_add_series_list(series)
```

Hover over a point to read its measurement in centimeters. Highcharts scales
each axis independently. A constant column keeps its value, and a missing
measurement leaves a gap in that flower's line.

## Boxplots

To compare petal lengths across species, let the helper calculate one box
per group. With `add_outliers = TRUE`, it also returns the scatter series
for the observations beyond the whiskers.

```{r boxplots}
boxes <- data_to_boxplot(iris, Petal.Length, Species, add_outliers = TRUE)

highchart() |>
  hc_xAxis(categories = levels(iris$Species)) |>
  hc_yAxis(title = list(text = "Petal length (cm)")) |>
  hc_add_series_list(boxes)
```

## Sankey links

Each row below is one visit. Column order defines the stages, and repeated
transitions increase the link weight. For example, three visits went from
Home to Search.

```{r sankey-links}
visits <- data.frame(
  landing = c("Home", "Home", "Home", "Offer"),
  next_page = c("Search", "Search", "Search", "Product"),
  outcome = c("Order", "Exit", "Order", "Order")
)

links <- data_to_sankey(visits)
hchart(links, type = "sankey", name = "Visits")
```

## Hierarchy nodes

The built-in `Titanic` table already contains counts. Sum `Freq` within
passenger class and survival status to size each leaf. The same nodes can
also be used in a sunburst. Each passenger class takes a color from the chart
theme, which its survival groups inherit. To keep fixed colors across themes,
pass a palette to `colors` in `data_to_hierarchical()`.

```{r hierarchy-nodes}
passengers <- as.data.frame(Titanic)
nodes <- data_to_hierarchical(passengers, c(Class, Survived), Freq)
hchart(nodes, type = "treemap")
```

## Annotation labels

Start with a chart and give each label an `x`, a `y` and its `text`. The
axis positions for this numeric series start at zero, so `x = 2` labels its
third point.

```{r annotation-labels}
notes <- data.frame(x = 2, y = 8, text = "Peak")
highchart() |>
  hc_add_series(data = c(3, 5, 8, 6)) |>
  hc_add_annotation(labels = data_to_annotation_labels(notes))
```

The same helper can label summits on an elevation profile. Stage 8 of the 2017
Tour de France ran from Dole to Station des Rousses. The profile and the
published summit positions come from [the original annotated example](https://jkunst.com/blog/posts/2020-06-02-30diasdegraficos-parte-3/).
[Download the elevation profile (CSV)](data/tour-2017-stage-8.csv).

```{r tour-elevation}
stage <- read.csv("data/tour-2017-stage-8.csv")
summits <- data.frame(
  x = c(101.44, 138.5, 176.4),
  y = c(1026, 748, 1202),
  text = c(
    "Col de la Joux",
    "Côte de Viry",
    "Montée de la Combe de Laisia Les Molunes"
  )
)

hchart(
  stage,
  "area",
  hcaes(distance, elevation),
  name = "Elevation",
  fillOpacity = 0.25
) |>
  hc_title(text = "Tour de France 2017 · Stage 8") |>
  hc_xAxis(title = list(text = "Distance (km)")) |>
  hc_yAxis(title = list(text = "Elevation (m)")) |>
  hc_tooltip(valueSuffix = " m") |>
  hc_add_annotation(labels = data_to_annotation_labels(summits))
```
